title: Convolve Two Signals
prompt:
Compute the linear convolution of

    x = [1, 4, -2]
    h = [2, 0]

Enter the result as a space-separated row.
hint: y[n] = Σ x[k]·h[n−k]; length is len(x)+len(h)−1
recap:
Linear convolution y[n] = Σₖ x[k]·h[n−k] flips h, slides it across x, and sums the overlap — exactly the output of an LTI system with impulse response h. Length is len(x)+len(h)−1.

Example — x = [1, 2, 3], h = [1, 1]: y = [1, 1+2, 2+3, 3] = [1, 3, 5, 3].

Convolution in time is multiplication in frequency (the convolution theorem), which the FFT exploits. Reference: Oppenheim & Schafer, Discrete-Time Signal Processing, ch. 2.
